newsitem.title: GERMANY: German FinMin says new borrowing 14.3 bln DM in Q1.
newsitem.headline: German FinMin says new borrowing 14.3 bln DM in Q1.

text.p: Germany's federal government borrowed a net 14.3 billion marks in the first quarter out of its targetted 53.4 billion mark budget deficit for the full year 1997, the Finance Ministry said on Friday.

A ministry spokesman said a claim by the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) that the first quarter federal deficit hit 40 billion marks in fact referred to the Bonn government's cash position, as already reported this week by the Bundesbank.
The spokesman added it was not possible to take the cash deficit from the first few months of the year as a basis for extrapolating the budget deficit for the whole year.
He said payments into the European Union budget had been made early, while petrol tax revenues in the new year had been below past levels due to changes in payment dates.

"This will have no impact on the full-year result," the spokesman said. Earlier, SPD finance spokesman Karl Diller said in a statement that Bonn had in the first quarter run up a deficit equal to three-quarters of the amount budgeted for this year and risked exhausting its credit.

Germany's federal budget deficit forms the largest chunk of its total public sector deficit, which Finance Minister Theo Waigel has said he wants to cut to 105 billion marks this year. That would be equivalent to 2.9 percent of GDP, and just inside the three percent limit set by the Maastricht treaty on European monetary union.
